thread.title: Intraday Update: Dow Drops 200 Points as Yields Rise…and Rise…and Rise - Barron's

title: Intraday Update: Dow Drops 200 Points as Yields Rise…and Rise…and Rise - Barron's
text:
May 15, 2018 1:13 p.m. ET
Oh, brother. Illustration: Bloomberg News
Interest rates are up and stocks are down.
The yield on the 10-year Treasury note—the most important single figure in the financial world—charged through the 3% threshold without blinking Tuesday morning, rising a full 0.07 percentage point to a four-year high of 3.06%.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell more than 200 points, while the broader Standard & Poor’s 500 fell 0.7%. Small-caps were little changed, with the Russell 2000 easing 0.1%
The really ominous news? The yield on three-month Treasury bills just jumped above that on the S&P 500 for the first time since the financial crisis 10 years ago. In other words, you can earn higher income on risk-free short-term money than you can on stocks. (For the curious, T-bills yield 1.93%, the S&P, 1.91%.)
John Lynch, chief investment strategist at LPL Financial, points out that the blue chips have just completed a terrific earnings season . Yet we have to ask: If the Federal Reserve’s policy of quantitative easing was good for stocks, shouldn’t the reverse policy—aka “quantitative tightening”—be bad for them?
Rising interest rates are the flip side of strong economic growth. New data Tuesday morning showed strong retail sales and homebuilder confidence .
In other news, the Argentine peso plunged yet again amid the country’s latest financial crisis. Startling fact: In the late 19th century, Argentina was one of the richest countries in the world. Now that’s impressive financial management for you.
Among the most popular stocks, Apple (AAPL) fell 1% and Tesla (TSLA) 3%. Facebook (FB) fell 1.5%, Netflix (NFLX), 1.25%, and Amazon.com (AMZN) and Alphabet (GOOGL) about 2% each.
S&P 500 : -0.8% to 2709.08 Dow 30 : -206.40 points, or 0.8%, to 24,693.01 Nasdaq : -0.9% to 7342.57 10-year Treasury Yield : +0.08 percentage point to 3.07% Midday Movers
Agilent Technologies (A) is down 7.9% to $63.77 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The instrument maker earned 65 cents a share, a penny above consensus estimates, on revenue of $1.21 billion, matching analysts' expectations. However, for the full year it expects to earn between $2.63 and $2.67 a share, compared with the $2.70 per-share consensus.
Cowen's Ryan Blicker calls the selloff a buying opportunity and upgrades Agilent to Outperform from Market Perform. "While Q2 wasn't an exciting quarter, we don't think the underlying outlook or thesis has changed, and continue to believe Agilent will grow revenue/EPS above peers for the foreseeable future (and likely exceed revised guidance)," he writs. "At ~$63, the stock is trading at a 5-10% EBITDA discount. We'd be buyers."
Boeing (BA) is down 0.7% to $342.17 after the World Trade Organization ruled that the European Union provided more than $22 billion in illegal subsidies to rival Airbus (EADSY).
CBS (CBS) is up 1.1% to $54.25 after Bernstein upgraded it to Outperform.
Hanesbrands (HBI) is up 3.2% to $17.27 after it reaffirmed its and full-year guidance at its investor day. The apparel maker expects to earn between $1.72 and $1.80 a share, on revenue of $6.72 billion to $6.82 billion. Analysts are looking for earnings of $1.76 a share on revenue of $6.77 billion.
US Foods (USFD) is up 1.1% to $35.45 after Morgan Stanley upgraded it to Overweight. — Teresa Rivas
